System

Guaranteed/random loot, corpse access and replay safety

A defeated creature yields a server-created loot allocation with guaranteed entries and weighted rolls. The allocation is generated once per defeat/recipient policy; opening the corpse again never rerolls rarity or produces a second entitlement.

Scope and player interaction

A defeated creature yields a server-created loot allocation with guaranteed entries and weighted rolls. The allocation is generated once per defeat/recipient policy; opening the corpse again never rerolls rarity or produces a second entitlement.

StageMeaning
First integration: Phase10committed; full feature contract may include explicitly staged later extensions
EvidenceAuthored implementation specification; no native/Blueprint/backend runtime verified

UI state machine

Unavailable → Generating → Available → ClaimPending → PartiallyClaimed → Empty → Expired

WBP_Loot observes results from URPGLootComponent. Pending is not Accepted. Close/cancel clears local focus and stale callbacks, but cannot undo an already committed backend command.

Definitions, fields and units

Canonical definition: DA_Loot_Mossfang. Stable IDs, quantities, seconds and centimeters are validated by the owner, not inferred from translated labels or sprites.

Field / rule
LootAllocationId UUID; DefeatId and RecipientCharacterId unique under personal-loot policy
GuaranteedEntries: item IDs and bounded integer quantities
WeightedPools: nonnegative weights, no-drop entry optional, roll count bounded
ResolvedEntries: definition/instance IDs, rolled affixes and currency stored once
AccessPolicy: eligible personal allocation; party rule snapshotted at defeat
ClaimedEntryIds and AllocationRevision: durable; corpse Actor is only a view
ExpiryUtc: cleanup policy; unclaimed rewards do not automatically reappear

C++ / Blueprint / backend ownership

LayerResponsibility
URPGLootComponentImplement the native validated request/state lifecycle described below; native runtime state is not editable by UMG.
Blueprint/Data AssetsTune the declared defaults and visual/asset assignments. Keep definition references EditDefaultsOnly/BlueprintReadOnly; cosmetic hooks cannot grant rewards.
Zone serverValidate live actor ownership, range/LOS, alive/action state, cooldown/tool/target rules and current session epoch where relevant.
BackendFor durable changes, revalidate trusted catalog/revision/ownership and commit records/source claims/receipt atomically. Read-only/cosmetic features have no durable mutation.
WBP_LootLocal observer/requester. Create only for local player; bind once, refresh immediately, unbind on teardown.

Custom command contracts

These names are project custom APIs or backend proposals, not existing Unreal/PaperZD nodes. Economic/backend requests are asynchronous; Pending resolves through the same command ID. Pure local queries are synchronous unless noted.

Command / result
MaterializeLoot(DefeatId, EligibilitySnapshot) -> AllocationIds|AlreadyGenerated
RequestOpenLoot(TargetActor) -> AccessibleView|NotEligible|TooFar
ClaimLoot(CommandId, AllocationId, EntryIds, ExpectedRevision) -> Granted|NoSpace|AlreadyClaimed
ExpireLoot(AllocationId) -> Expired|StillActive; server/backend policy

End-to-end command and observation flow

  1. Committed defeat ledger provides eligibility and loot-table version. Validate every item/family ID before enabling the encounter.
  2. Server/backend selects each guaranteed and weighted outcome once, recording resolved entries and random audit context without exposing secret seeds to clients.
  3. Replicate the existence/available state of the corpse and send only the eligible player their loot details. An optional visible pickup references the same allocation entry, not a second reward.
  4. Player chooses entries; server repeats range, ownership and current allocation checks and submits one claim command.
  5. Database transaction locks allocation and inventory, checks capacity, transfers exact entries/currency and marks them claimed with receipt/revision. NoSpace leaves unclaimed entries intact.
  6. UI displays committed inventory result and remaining allocation. Corpse reload/reconnect queries existing allocation, never invokes generation again.

Editor configuration and real consumers

  1. Create URPGLootDefinition and DA_Loot_Mossfang with guaranteed cloth scrap plus one weighted pool. Use test weights CommonMaterial=90, RareToken=9, NoDrop=1 only as a fixture.
  2. Create BP_LootContainer with interaction interface and stable allocation reference. Enemy corpse can use it directly or spawn a view actor; choose one representation path per entry.
  3. Build WBP_Loot with entry selection, take-all, pending/rejected states and clear ownership text.
  4. Reopen FinalizeDefeat to create/trigger the allocation exactly once after eligible defeat commit; reopen inventory capacity service and owner snapshot observer.
  5. Place two clients at one corpse, one eligible and one unrelated, plus a full-bag fixture. Restore the same corpse from persisted state for reload testing.

Reopen Phase10 integration entries after creating the assets. Test fixture: L_Rillmere / Corpse_Mossfang_01 / Party_AB. No later-phase runtime dependency should be activated before its recorded integration phase.

Failure, contention and recovery acceptance

Test stimulus and expected result
Unrelated character opens personal allocation -> NotEligible; no entry details leaked.
Claim replay -> original result/AlreadyClaimed, no extra item.
Full bag -> NoSpace with allocation unchanged; currency-only claims follow explicit separate entry selection.
Missing loot item definition -> encounter content validation fails or loot quarantined with MissingLootDefinition, never substitute an arbitrary reward.
Corpse expires after UI opens -> Expired; no partial item transfer.

Repeat the success route with two clients when networking exists, then disconnect immediately before/after a committed result. Query the same command and compare authoritative snapshot/receipt with UI. Restart the relevant zone, reject stale epochs, and rerun the previous phase route. Pure visual/input features instead verify cleanup and unchanged server facts. These are future test recipes, not reported passes.

Tuning, accessibility and observability

Personal loot is the initial simple group policy. Need/greed, master loot or shared roll UI are later rule changes requiring abuse/timeout tests. Rarity weights are content tuning, not UI constants.

Audit table version, allocation, recipient, resolved item IDs and claim receipt. Track unclaimed expiry, rare-item issuance and duplicate-claim suppression.

Art gaps, production and do-not-build-yet

The asset ZIP and installed PaperZD APIs remain unverified. Required new art/unsupported layer combinations are tracked in art/animation-matrix.html and art/equipment-visual-matrix.html. A legal debug visual can prove authority but is not finished content. Production features listed as later/optional remain disabled until their phase/gate passes.
